I've been thinking about going to an Appleseed shoot to learn the fundamentals of rifle marksmanship. I've heard mixed reviews from people and from what I've gathered they teach you how to shoot, but some of the methods are obsolete today. Is it worth it?
Anyone Ever Gone to an Appleseed Shoot?

I haven't been but would love to. imo learning to and practicing with iron sights will never be out dated. At the very least you'll pick up a tip or two. Maybe meet some like minded people. Worst case scenario it's an excuse to put rounds down range.

I'm planning to go early next year. I like the idea of going as a beginner especially because you get to practice shooting with a bunch of extra variables taken out. Shooting 22lr at 25 yards is the equivalent of not having to account for drop, wind, elevation, temperature, and most importantly, recoil.

All position, breathing, trigger, natural point of aim, sight picture and a bunch of ammo to reinforce those good habits. You can learn ballistics later and use bigger/faster bullets to shoot further but it's all moot if you have poor fundamentals. People spend so much money and even more time researching the "best" rifle, caliber, and sometimes scopes but you can't buy good principles; they are developed through repetition.
